input.summary:
parts/room-18.mjs ("room: west upper corridor") now writes nothing: its layout (console, chair, bench, barrels, runner, lanterns, candles) is kept as data but not placed.
All 26 of its furniture writes were refused, because mansion shell box() fills the whole interior with air and runParts locks every cell an earlier part set, air included. Nothing was off-palette.
./make.sh now prints "west upper corridor: 0 placed" with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE and writes build.nbt.
left: The part is not built: the corridor's furniture is missing from build.nbt. Restoring it needs the shell or the lock to change, which is outside this module.

Root cause is in parts/shell.mjs box() (fill(..., "air") over the interior, lines ~26-28): every interior air cell becomes owned by the shell. Fix there by leaving interior cells unset instead of air, or by letting later parts write into air. Both are outside room-18.

Once that is fixed, restore the layers(g, ORIGIN, LEGEND, [Y11, Y12, Y13, EMPTY, EMPTY, Y16]) call in build(g) and re-run make.sh. The same block should hold for every other room part, since they share the air lock.
parts-report.json lists only the first 8 refused cells per part, so the full set was counted from the 26 non-space cells in the layers rows rather than read from the report.

waste.what: Worked out by hand that every furniture cell was owned by the shell, by reading build.mjs's runParts lock and shell.mjs's box() fill; the report never says which earlier part owns a refused cell.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls reading library and shell source; 26 refused cells traced by counting the non-space characters in the layers rows
waste.tool: A preflight in `mcd plan` / `runParts` that prints, per room, how many of its cells are free and which earlier part owns each blocked cell (for example 'owned by shell box() air'). Also list every refused cell in parts-report.json, not the first 8.

waste.what: Decided between removing the writes and leaving the file unchanged, and checked that no cell in the room box was free to move the writes to.
waste.cost: one judgement call, one extra grep over the shell
waste.tool: A `mcd free <room> --rooms rooms.json` that reports unclaimed cells in the room box. It would have shown zero free cells in one call, without reading source.

companions.task: Change the masonry shell's box() so interior cells are left unset (or marked as room space) rather than filled with air; that lets the room fit-outs place furniture on the floor cells they own.
Once the interior is free, check the dark oak console, bench and chair in the west upper corridor for fit and walkability, then restore the furniture layout.
